proofs.full_local_argument:
All logarithms are natural. Fix d,T>=1, L,r>0 and S containing [-r,r]^d. For alpha in {-1,+1}^d, a>0 and 0<delta<=1/4 define F_alpha(x)=(a/d)sum_i[(1/2+alpha_i delta)|x_i+r|+(1/2-alpha_i delta)|x_i-r|] on all R^d and restrict to S. Convexity follows from nonnegative weights. Each coordinate has absolute slope at most a/d, so Holder gives |F_alpha(x)-F_alpha(y)|<=a d^(1/p-1)||x-y||_q, including endpoints p=1,infinity. Each scalar mixture is minimized at -r alpha_i, giving x*_alpha=-r alpha in S and min F_alpha=ar(1-2delta). Thus arbitrary extra points of S cannot lower the minimum. On [-r,r], the scalar contribution before a/d is r+2alpha_i delta x_i. Outside this interval its value increases away from the nearest endpoint. Decode alpha_i by the sign opposite to x_i, choosing +1 at x_i=0. Whenever this decoder is wrong, the i-th contribution to F_alpha(x)-min F_alpha is at least 2a delta r/d. This holds also outside the cube, without projecting an Algorithm query.

Define the following legal Oracles once for the entire finite family. Oracle A samples I uniform on [d], B~Bernoulli(1/2+alpha_I delta), independently afresh conditional on alpha each call; return h_A(x)=a[B|x_I+r|+(1-B)|x_I-r|] and a subgradient of that same sampled function. Fix derivative 0 at each absolute-value kink. Oracle B samples independent B_i with those biases and returns h_B(x)=(a/d)sum_i[B_i|x_i+r|+(1-B_i)|x_i-r|] and its similarly fixed subgradient. Finite averaging gives E h=F_alpha and E z in partial F_alpha, at boundary points as well. For A, ||z||_p<=a almost surely for every p. For B, ||z||_p<=a d^(1/p-1). Choose a=L for 1<=p<=2 with A, and a=L d^(1-1/p) for p>2 with B. In both cases the moment bound is <=L^2 and F_alpha is in the original F_cv. No value-noise variance condition is needed: Definition 1 only imposes unbiased values and the subgradient second moment. Distinct alpha give distinct functions since the cube has interior. Extend this single Oracle mapping to remaining attained-minimum functions in F_cv by exact value and a bounded subgradient: at interior points Lipschitz convexity gives a subgradient of p-norm<=L; at boundary points extend f from int S using a supporting affine functional and take a limiting bounded subgradient. Explicitly take interior x_n tending to x, choose bounded supporting slopes z_n there, extract a convergent subsequence, use Lipschitz continuity and the supporting inequalities for every y in S to obtain f(y)>=f(x)+z.(y-x). Thus the extension exists even for nonclosed S. The extension need not be computationally efficient; only its legal Oracle interface matters. This fixes phi before inf_M.

Here are the elementary statistical inequalities used, with their arguments. For finite positive laws P,Q let D(P||Q)=sum P log(P/Q) and TV(P,Q)=max_A|P(A)-Q(A)|. The log-sum inequality follows by convexity of u log u with Q weights. Grouping the terms of KL by an event A therefore gives D(P||Q)>=kl(P(A)||Q(A)). For fixed v, the second derivative of kl(u||v) in u is 1/[u(1-u)]>=4, with value and first derivative zero at u=v; hence kl(u||v)>=2(u-v)^2. Choose A={P>=Q} to obtain TV<=sqrt(D/2). Any equal-prior binary test, including a randomized one, has error at least (1-TV)/2: for a deterministic decision set the error is (1-P(A)+Q(A))/2; randomization is an average of such tests. A common random seed independent of the parameter does not increase TV, by averaging over its law.

For Bernoulli(1/2+delta) versus Bernoulli(1/2-delta), the KL in either direction is 2delta log((1+2delta)/(1-2delta)) <=8delta^2/(1-2delta)<=16delta^2, using log(1+u)<=u. Let Z denote the complete sequence of T revealed coin data, (I_t,B_t) for A or (B_{t,i}) for B. These observations are independent across calls conditional on fixed alpha, and their laws do not depend on the query points. For alpha,beta differing only in coordinate i, one-call KL is <=16delta^2/d for A and <=16delta^2 for B. Multiplying the positive product likelihoods and taking expectations gives D(P_alpha^Z||P_beta^Z)<=16Tdelta^2/d or 16Tdelta^2 respectively; this is conditional product KL, not marginal iid mutual information. Every adaptive Oracle transcript, its queries and x_T are deterministic functions of Z for a deterministic method. Any independent method seed can be included as additional parameter-independent randomness, though the recorded claim needs only the original convention. Thus any test decoded from x_T is also a test using Z; access to query-dependent values leaks no extra information beyond Z.

Average alpha uniformly on the full sign cube solely for this local proof. For each coordinate i and fixed other signs, pair the two possible alpha_i values. The preceding binary inequality bounds that pair's mean probability of sign error by at least (1-sqrt(8Tdelta^2/d))/2 for A and (1-sqrt(8Tdelta^2))/2 for B. Averaging the other signs and summing the nonnegative coordinate gaps proves that every M has average objective gap at least a delta r (1-sqrt(8Tdelta^2/d)) for A and a delta r (1-sqrt(8Tdelta^2)) for B. Sup_f is at least this finite average, for the one already fixed legal phi.

For A take delta=min{1/4,sqrt(d/(128T))}. Then sqrt(8Tdelta^2/d)<=1/4 and risk >=(3/4)Lr min{1/4,sqrt(d/T)/sqrt(128)}=min{3Lr/16,3Lr sqrt(d/T)/(4sqrt(128))}. Each term dominates the corresponding term in min{Lr sqrt(d/T)/10000,Lr/144}; hence so does the minimum. This covers all dimensions including d=1 without Lemma 4 or NY. For B take delta=1/sqrt(128T)<=1/4. Risk >=3Lr d^(1-1/p)/(4sqrt(128T)), which is >=Lr d^(1-1/p)/(10000sqrt(T)), and therefore >=min{that term,Lr d^(1-1/p)/72}. Take inf_M and then sup_phi to get exactly the assigned two branches with one universal c0=1/10000. Shifts +/-r and the minimum ar(1-2delta) were calculated directly; no p.18 scalar formula or added assumption is used. The full-cube proof device and these local parameter choices do not change the separately published Source or the normalized packed Hard Family.

assumptions: S is a convex subset of R^d containing B_infinity(r).
Standing Section 2.1 convention: the minimum is attained.
phi ranges over O_{p,L}: queries in S return joint (fhat,zhat) with E fhat(x)=f(x), E zhat(x) in partial f(x), E||zhat(x)||_p^2<=L^2.
M_T is the adaptive query class of Section 2.1; no span or coordinate-support restriction is imposed.
statement.conclusion: There exists a universal c0>0 (the local argument below permits c0=1/10000) such that sup_{phi in O_{p,L}}epsilon*_T(F_cv,S;phi)>=min{c0 L r sqrt(d/T),L r/144} for 1<=p<=2, and >=min{c0 L r d^(1-1/p)/sqrt(T),L r d^(1-1/p)/72} for 2<p<=infinity. These are the unchanged source Theorem 1 conclusions; the explicit value of c0 is local, not attributed to the source.
statement.objects_and_definitions: F_cv(S,L,p) consists of convex f:S->R with |f(x)-f(y)|<=L||x-y||_q for every x,y in S, q conjugate to p. epsilon*_T(F_cv,S;phi)=inf_{M in M_T}sup_{f in F_cv}E_phi[f(x_T)-min_{x in S}f(x)]; x_T is the final query point, not an arbitrary uncharged post-query output.
statement.parameter_domains: d,T positive integers; L,r>0; 1<=p<=infinity; 1/p+1/q=1 with endpoint conventions.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every positive integer d,T, every L,r>0, eligible convex S containing B_infinity(r), and p in [1,infinity], the bounds hold with one universal c0. Quantifier order is sup_phi inf_M sup_f E_phi, with last-query output x_T and source expectation over Oracle randomness. The proof fixes one legal Oracle mapping before taking inf_M. No transfer of the recorded output or expectation convention is required.
